It doesn't.
To summarize, for anybody fixing, since I didn't know this yesterday, Forward+ and Mobile keep choosing D3D12 forcibly regardless of any settings or even startup commands, as visible in the cmd panel + verbose setting.
As a tip for anybody with this issue stumbling upon this page, I heavily recommend either regressing to 4.5 or porting a project from 4.5, running it in Forward+ and changing to compatibility.
How are you forcing Vulkan? I can't replicate it always choosing D3D12

Can you try these steps?

Open an Administrator PowerShell window and run the following command:

```
Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name "Tools.Graphics.DirectX~~~~0.0.1.0"
```

This'll install D3D12 debug layers so we can figure out what's going on. It might take a while to complete.

Then download and run dbgview64.exe:

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/debugview

Afterwards, run Godot in the command line with the following arguments:

```
--rendering-driver d3d12 --gpu-validation
```

When you see CreatePipelineState errors, DbgView should print details about what went wrong. Please show these here.

@blueskythlikesclouds It seems it can't find D3D12's SDK, D3D12Core.dll is in system32, which is where it should be. As for 'forcing' Vulkan, I meant setting all the driver settings in the project to use Vulkan and disabling the D3D12 fallback, I'm 'forcing' it to not use D3D12. Hmm, it doesn't look like the debug layers got enabled. Otherwise, you should have seen D3D12 related messages. Did you open your project from the project manager? Maybe the command line options don't get transferred to it. 

If you did that, could you point at your project's folder with `--path` option to open it without going through the project manager first? Include `--rendering-driver d3d12 --gpu-validation` options too, of course.

---

> It seems it can't find D3D12's SDK, D3D12Core.dll is in system32, which is where it should be.

These errors are for the Agility SDK specifically. It's looking for D3D12Core.dll placed next to the Godot executable, which is included in CI builds but not the official releases.
I'm sorry, you're gonna have to walk me throw the pointing at the project folder part.

Sure. You can drag and drop the folder of your Godot project from Explorer to the command line, and it'll automatically paste its path there. You should have something like this (example from my Windows PC):

```
C:\Users\Skyth\Downloads\Godot_v4.6-stable_win64.exe --rendering-driver d3d12 --gpu-validation --path "C:\Repositories\tps-demo"
```

running `C:\Users\hp\Downloads\Godot_v4.6-stable_win64.exe\Godot_v4.6-stable_win64_console.exe --rendering-driver d3d12 --gpu-validation --path "C:\Personal\godot\new-game-project" ` in admin perm powershell works as long as you have a main scene designated, it does not bug out and gives the default grey, however, a test scene with a camera and a csg box also net the default grey, meaning it's not actually rendering anything. During two tests, DebugView net a similar error to last time. I have no idea what OBS is other than the recorder (which isn't active) and whoever snuck a quick hl1 ref in there.

What about when you run the editor? Including `--editor` command line option should do the trick.
I don't know why OBS would be trying to hook itself to Godot in D3D12, that normally only happens with Vulkan.

The "Unable to load D3D12Core.dll" error is fine, you can ignore that.

Yes, that driver is way too old. I doubt it but maybe you can download more recent drivers from AMD's own website.
Since you mentioned you are always forced to D3D12, it sounds like you cannot create a Vulkan device either. It might be best that we redirect these drivers for old devices to Compatibility.
Which is weird? Like, other games and softwares that use both D3D12 and Vulkan are entirely fine? Godot is the only one with this issue.

Previously closed this issue because a driver update seemed to fix _a_ part of the issue, but did not thoroughly test it enough.
Projects that were ported from 4.5 to 4.6 now seem to run fine, but new projects still cannot run, and exported Godot projects also do not run.

D3D12 and Vulkan run in other applications like we established (maybe bluesky forgot?), but don't run specifically with Godot new or exported 4.6 projects.

I want to note, exported projects still play sound and don't have the unresponsiveness issue of the editor, the image I posted of the glitchy pattern moves and changes (as if the renderer is trying), 4.5 projects are fine.

I'll ask like I did before for somebody to tell me if they know a way to force Vulkan to play a project.

Okay, so further testing with a slightly more stable 4.6: You can port a project from 4.5 to 4.6, it'll run entirely bugless and will be indistinguishable from regular 4.5 (though I haven't tested it for an extended period of time). Turning off fallback to _both_ Vulkan and D3D12 _and_ manually setting the driver (as far as I know? unless I'm writing this wrong) to OpenGL still uses D3D12 on _new_ projects. I can't stress hard enough that both Vulkan and D3D12 work fine everywhere else _including_ previous Godot versions but don't work in 4.6 and consistently force the renderer to use D3D12. I don't have any indication that Godot's actually trying to fallback to Vulkan, so I'd say the computer not being able to run Vulkan is a bit of a jump. As for running _other_ people's Godot projects, adding --rendering-driver opengl3 **or** --rendering-driver vulkan at the end of the Target property seems to force it to use either, which adds confirmation that the computer can use Vulkan (even if boot up is slower).

These old integrated graphics only support Direct3D 12 with a limited feature level. Running Godot 4's Forward+/Mobile on it is always going to be challenging, not to mention the limited processing power makes Compatibility a better fit for those integrated graphics anyway.

Unfortunately, most engine contributors don't have access to such a GPU, so we can't bisect the exact commit that caused the regression. We need to know this to even start into looking into fixing the issue.

You can look into [bisecting the regression](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/feedback/bisecting.html) yourself, which would be very appreciated, but I understand it would take a lot of time to compile Godot several times on an old CPU. To save some time in bisecting, you can also try reproducing the bug in all [pre-release 4.6 versions](https://godotengine.org/download/archive/) (from dev1 to rc2), and report the first version where the regression occurred here. This will already greatly narrow down the range of builds to compile.

What we can do as a stopgap is force old GPUs to fallback to Compatibility, even if they *in theory* support Direct3D or Vulkan. This will at least prevent the engine from crashing on startup, or displaying broken visuals.

PS: If you want to check the Vulkan version actually supported by your driver, download the [Vulkan Hardware Capability Viewer](https://vulkan.gpuinfo.org/download.php) and run it.

I have some ideas why. Can you note some D3D12 games that run fine on your system?

D3D12 isn't rigid. It received many new features and updates over the years. Godot makes use of them. It's possible that the games you can run keep themselves limited to the decade old features.
Aforementioned Animal well, I've played some logged 1200+ games and I'm sure some of them were bound to use D3D12, recently used PCSX2 to no error.
